nodes.name: Schedule - Daily
nodes.notes: 09:30, after everything else has run and had a chance to fail. 05:00 FX -> 06:00 KPI -> 07:00 detect -> 07:30 decide -> 08:00 explain -> 08:30 deliver -> 09:00 execute -> 09:30 clean up after all of it.

nodes.name: Manual Run
nodes.notes: On-demand run, for during an incident. Same path as the schedule and equally safe to repeat.

nodes.name: Open Maintenance Run

parameters.query:
-- Open the run ledger entry. Shared table, source='operational-maintenance'.
--
-- Maintenance uses the same ledger as every other pipeline, deliberately: a
-- maintenance run that crashed is exactly the kind of stuck 'running' row this
-- workflow exists to find, and it should be able to find its own.
--
-- The window is today. Maintenance is not about a data window; the columns are
-- NOT NULL, so they say when rather than pretending to say what.
INSERT INTO salesops.ingestion_runs
    (batch_id, source, window_from, window_to, status, n8n_execution_id)
VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), 'operational-maintenance',
        CURRENT_DATE, CURRENT_DATE, 'running', $1)
RETURNING
    batch_id::text AS batch_id,
    run_id,
    -- The state of the world before anything is recovered, so the finalize node
    -- can report what changed rather than only what is left.
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.ingestion_runs
      WHERE status = 'running'
        AND started_at < now() - make_interval(mins => salesops.operational_setting('stale_run_timeout_minutes')::int)
    )::int                                                      AS stale_runs_before,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.remediation_actions
      WHERE status = 'executing')::int                          AS executing_before,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.ingestion_replay_candidates
      WHERE replay_eligible)::int                               AS replay_candidates_before,
    (SELECT overall_status FROM salesops.operational_health_summary) AS health_before;

nodes.notes: Opens ingestion_runs with source='operational-maintenance' and snapshots the state of the world before anything is recovered.

nodes.name: Recover Stale Runs

parameters.query:
-- Close runs abandoned at 'running' past the configured timeout.
--
-- RECOVERY, NOT RE-EXECUTION. The work is not repeated. Whether it should be
-- is a separate question with a different answer per pipeline - the ingestion
-- window self-heals on the next run, Stages 5-8 are idempotent, and Stage 9
-- needs a human. This only stops the ledger lying about what is in flight.
--
-- This run's own row is younger than the timeout, so it cannot recover itself.
SELECT
    count(*)::int                                              AS recovered,
    COALESCE(string_agg(source || '#' || run_id, ', '), 'none') AS detail
FROM salesops.recover_stale_runs('stage10-recovery', FALSE);

nodes.notes: Branch 1 of 5. onError=continueRegularOutput: these five operations are unrelated, and one being impossible says nothing about whether the others are. A maintenance workflow that abandoned the rest of its work on the first error would be a reliability feature that reduces reliability.

nodes.name: Recover Stale Remediation

parameters.query:
-- Move remediation actions stranded at 'executing' into 'execution_unknown'.
--
-- THIS CALLS NO PROVIDER, and that is the entire point. A process that died
-- around a provider call may have completed the external call first. Both
-- automatic answers are wrong: re-executing might do the thing twice, failing
-- it might claim something did not happen when it did.
--
-- So the uncertainty is recorded rather than resolved. 'execution_unknown' is
-- absent from remediation_pending_execution, so nothing picks it up
-- automatically, and the only way out is a human reconciling it.
SELECT
    count(*)::int                                                  AS recovered,
    COALESCE(string_agg(remediation_id::text, ', '), 'none')        AS detail,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.remediation_actions
      WHERE status = 'execution_unknown')::int                      AS awaiting_reconciliation
FROM salesops.recover_stale_remediation('stage10-recovery', FALSE);

nodes.notes: Branch 2 of 5. Never re-executes. An action whose outcome nobody knows is moved to a state that says so, and a human reconciles it.

nodes.name: Collect Operational Signals

parameters.query:
-- Review ageing and replay candidates. READ-ONLY, both of them.
--
-- Ageing changes no review state, ever. "Nobody has looked at this" is not a
-- decision, and a maintenance run that resolved, dismissed or approved an item
-- because it got old would be making one on a human's behalf.
--
-- Replay candidates are reported, not replayed. Replay is the one maintenance
-- operation that repeats work, so it stays an explicit act.
--
-- These are operational ageing labels. They are NOT anomaly severity and are
-- not comparable with it: a critical anomaly reviewed within the hour is a
-- healthy pipeline, and a minor one unclaimed for a week is not.
SELECT
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.review_ageing)::int                          AS open_reviews,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.review_ageing WHERE ageing_bucket = 'warning')::int
                                                                                AS reviews_warning,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.review_ageing WHERE ageing_bucket = 'overdue')::int
                                                                                AS reviews_overdue,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.review_ageing
      WHERE ageing_bucket = 'critical_overdue')::int                            AS reviews_critical_overdue,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.review_ageing WHERE escalation_eligible)::int AS reviews_escalatable,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.ingestion_replay_candidates
      WHERE replay_eligible)::int                                               AS replay_candidates,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.stale_notifications)::int                    AS stale_notifications,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.operational_retry_queue WHERE retry_eligible)::int
                                                                                AS retry_eligible,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.operational_retry_queue WHERE terminal)::int  AS terminal_failures,
    0                                                                           AS review_state_changes;

nodes.notes: Branch 3 of 5. Read-only. review_state_changes is hardcoded 0 and asserted by the test suite: ageing must never change a review's state.

nodes.name: Staging Retention

parameters.query:
-- Delete settled staging rows past the retention period.
--
-- Only 'processed' and 'skipped' rows are ever eligible. 'pending' is
-- unfinished work; 'failed' is the dead-letter trail, and deleting it would
-- destroy both the replay source and the record that something went wrong.
-- Neither is a rule this node has to remember - purge_staging() enforces both,
-- and a row involved in a replay is protected by a foreign key on top.
--
-- Retaining every failed row forever is stricter than a retention policy needs
-- to be. It is also the only default that cannot lose evidence.
--
-- Idempotent: a second run finds nothing left to delete.
SELECT
    rows_eligible::int   AS eligible,
    rows_deleted::int    AS deleted,
    rows_protected::int  AS protected,
    retention_days,
    cutoff
FROM salesops.purge_staging(FALSE, 'stage10-recovery');

nodes.notes: Branch 4 of 5. Runs for real (dry_run=FALSE) because the eligibility rules are conservative enough to be safe unattended: pending and failed rows are never eligible, and neither is anything involved in a replay.

nodes.name: Retry Stale Notifications
nodes.notes: Branch 5 of 5. The only step needing the service: retrying a stale notification means asking Stage 8 to route again for that date, using its own delivery path, idempotency key and attempt accounting. Re-implementing any of that here would create a second delivery path to disagree with the first. NO CREDENTIALS HERE - the webhook URL and recipient list live in the service environment. purge and replay are false: this call is for the notification step, and the SQL branches above own the rest. A notification already 'sent' cannot be touched, because resend is never set.

nodes.name: Finalize Maintenance Run

parameters.query:
-- Close the run, deriving the status from what the branches actually did.
--
-- 'failed'  every branch failed. Nothing was recovered and nothing was
--           cleaned up; the pipeline is in exactly the state it was.
--
-- 'partial' some branches failed and others did real work. Reported honestly
--           rather than as success, because a caller reading only the status
--           has to be able to trust it.
--
-- 'success' every branch that ran completed - including the common case where
--           there was nothing to recover, which is a healthy pipeline rather
--           than a wasted run.
--
-- records_received  = maintenance branches attempted
-- records_accepted  = branches that completed
-- records_rejected  = branches that failed
-- records_duplicate = 0 (a branch has one outcome; there is no third state)
-- The four balance by construction, satisfying the counts CHECK.
UPDATE salesops.ingestion_runs r
SET finished_at       = now(),
    records_received  = $2::int,
    records_accepted  = $2::int - $3::int,
    records_rejected  = $3::int,
    records_duplicate = 0,
    status            = CASE
                            WHEN $3::int >= $2::int THEN 'failed'
                            WHEN $3::int > 0        THEN 'partial'
                            ELSE 'success'
                        END,
    error_message     = CASE WHEN $3::int > 0
                             THEN $3::text || ' maintenance branch(es) failed: ' || $4::text
                        END
WHERE r.batch_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING
    run_id,
    batch_id::text AS batch_id,
    status,
    $2::int        AS branches_attempted,
    $3::int        AS branches_failed,
    $5::int        AS stale_runs_recovered,
    $6::int        AS stale_remediation_recovered,
    $7::int        AS staging_rows_deleted,
    -- The state of the world after. Compared against the 'before' snapshot
    -- taken by the opening node, this is what makes a rerun's idempotency
    -- readable straight from the ledger.
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.ingestion_runs
      WHERE status = 'running'
        AND started_at < now() - make_interval(mins => salesops.operational_setting('stale_run_timeout_minutes')::int)
    )::int                                                          AS stale_runs_after,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.remediation_actions
      WHERE status = 'execution_unknown')::int                      AS awaiting_reconciliation,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.operational_retry_queue WHERE retry_eligible)::int
                                                                    AS retry_eligible,
    (SELECT overall_status FROM salesops.operational_health_summary) AS health_after,
    (SELECT array_to_string(unhealthy, ', ')
       FROM salesops.operational_health_summary)                     AS unhealthy_components,
    round(extract(epoch FROM (finished_at - started_at))::numeric, 2) AS duration_seconds;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ (() => { const names = ['Recover Stale Runs','Recover Stale Remediation','Collect Operational Signals','Staging Retention','Retry Stale Notifications']; const get = n => { try { return $(n).first().json; } catch (e) { return { error: 'node did not run' }; } }; const results = names.map(n => ({ name: n, json: get(n) })); const failed = results.filter(r => r.json && r.json.error); return [ $('Open Maintenance Run').first().json.batch_id, results.length, failed.length, failed.map(f => f.name + ' (' + ((f.json.error && (f.json.error.message || f.json.error.description)) || 'failed') + ')').join('; ').slice(0, 400) || 'none', get('Recover Stale Runs').recovered || 0, get('Recover Stale Remediation').recovered || 0, get('Staging Retention').deleted || 0 ]; })() }}

nodes.notes: Aggregates all five branches. Status is derived from how many failed, never from having reached this node. Reads each branch defensively - a node that errored still produced an item, and the expression treats a missing result as a failed branch rather than throwing.
